title: Bench top CUT&Tag
author: Hatice S Kaya-Okur
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.bcuhiwt6
materials: NE1 buffer (for preparing nuclei) Mix 1 ml 1M HEPES-KOH pH 7.9, 500 μL 1M KCl, 12.5 μL 2 M spermidine, 500 µL 10% Triton X-100, and 10 ml glycerol in 38 ml dH 2 O, and add 1 Roche Complete Protease Inhibitor EDTA-Free Digitonin (5%) Dissolve 50 mg digitonin in 1 ml DMSO. Hold at room temperature for up to 1 week, or freeze at -20 °C. When using native or fixed nuclei prepared in Triton-X100, digitonin may be omitted from all solutions. Caution: Digitonin is toxic and care should be taken especially when weighing out the powder. Use full PPE including a mask, lab coat and gloves while handling any amount of digitonin. Be aware that DMSO can penetrate through the skin. Binding buffer Mix 200 μL 1M HEPES pH 7.9, 100 μL 1M KCl, 10 μL 1M CaCl 2 and 10 μL 1M MnCl 2 , and bring the final volume to 10 mL with dH 2 O. Store the buffer at 4 °C for 6 months. Wash buffer Mix 1 mL 1 M HEPES pH 7.5, 1.5 mL 5 M NaCl, 12.5 μL 2 M spermidine, bring the final volume to 50 mL with dH 2 O, and add 1 Roche Complete Protease Inhibitor EDTA-Free tablet. Store the buffer at 4 °C for up to 1 week. Dig-wash buffer (optional for nuclei) Mix 400 μL 5% digitonin with 40 mL Wash buffer. Store the buffer at 4 °C for up to 2 days. Antibody buffer Mix 8 μL 0.5 M EDTA and 6.7 µL 30% BSA with 2 mL Dig-wash buffer and chill on ice. Dig-300 buffer Mix 1 mL 1 M HEPES pH 7.5, 3 mL 5 M NaCl and 12.5 μL 2 M spermidine, bring the final volume to 50 mL with dH 2 O, and add 100 µL 5% digitonin (0.01%) and 1 Roche Complete Protease Inhibitor EDTA-Free tablet. Buffer without digitonin may be held for 1 week, but Digitonin should only be added the same day to minimize precipitation. Tagmentation buffer Mix 5 mL Dig-300 buffer and 50 µL 1 M MgCl 2 . Tn5-adapter complex formation: 1.Anneal each of Mosaic end - adapter A (ME-A) and Mosaic end - adapter B (ME-B) oligonucleotides with Mosaic end – reverse oligonucleotides. 2.To anneal, dilute oligonucleotides to 200 µM in annealing buffer (10mM Tris pH8, 50mM NaCl, 1 mM EDTA). Each pair of oligos, ME-A+ME-Reverse and ME-B+ME-Reverse, is mixed separately resulting in 100 µM annealed product. 3.Place the tubes in a 90-95°C hot block and leave for 3-5 minutes, then remove the hot block from the heat source allowing for slow cooling to room temperature (~45 minutes). 4.Mix 8 µL 100 µM preannealed ME-A and 8 µL 100 µM preannealed ME-B with 100 µL 5.5 µM pA-Tn5. 5.Incubate the mixture on a rotating platform for 1 hour at room temperature and then store at -20 °C.

steps.title: Prepare ConA bead slurry
steps.instruction: Gently resuspend the ConA bead stock and withdraw enough slurry to provide 10 µL per sample (10 µL × 16 samples = 160 µL). Transfer 170 µL of bead slurry into 1.6 mL Binding buffer in a 2 mL tube, mix by pipetting, place on a magnetic stand until the beads clear (30 s–2 min). Remove the supernatant, add 1.5 mL Binding buffer, mix, and remove any residual liquid from the cap with a quick pulse on a micro‑centrifuge. Place the tube on the magnet again, remove the liquid, and finally resuspend the beads in 170 µL Binding buffer (10 µL per future sample). Keep the bead slurry at room temperature until the cells are ready.

steps.title: Harvest and count cells
steps.instruction: Harvest fresh culture(s) in a 15 mL or 50 mL conical tube at room temperature, count cells, and use up to ~5 × 10⁵ cells per sample.

steps.title: Wash cells (unfixed)
steps.instruction: Centrifuge 3 min at 600 × g in a swinging‑bucket rotor at room temperature, discard supernatant, resuspend in 1 volume PBS at room temperature while pipetting, centrifuge again 3 min at 600 × g, discard supernatant, resuspend in ½ volume ice‑cold NE1 buffer, vortex gently, and sit on ice 10 min.

steps.title: Fix cells (optional)
steps.instruction: Centrifuge 4 min at 1300 × g at 4 °C, discard supernatant, add 16 % formaldehyde to a final concentration of 0.1 % (e.g., 62 µL to 10 mL), incubate at room temperature 2 min, quench with 1.25 M glycine to twice the molar amount of formaldehyde (e.g., 600 µL to 10 mL), centrifuge 4 min at 1300 × g at 4 °C, discard supernatant, and resuspend in Wash buffer to ~1 × 10⁶ cells · mL⁻¹.

steps.title: Optional nuclei freezing
steps.instruction: Aliquot 900 µL of nuclei suspension into cryogenic vials, add 100 µL DMSO, mix, place vials in a Mr. Frosty filled with isopropanol, freeze overnight at –80 °C, then store at –80 °C.

steps.title: Thaw frozen cells/nuclei
steps.instruction: Thaw frozen aliquots at room temperature (e.g., in a 20 mL beaker of water) and proceed to the bead‑binding step.

steps.title: Bind cells to ConA beads
steps.instruction: Retrieve the tube(s) containing cells or nuclei, vortex gently at ~1100 rpm, slowly add the prepared ConA bead slurry, and place on an end‑over‑end rotator for 5–10 min.

steps.title: Resuspend cells in Antibody buffer
steps.instruction: Resuspend the bead‑bound cells in 800 µL ice‑cold Antibody buffer, vortex gently, keep on ice, and divide into 16 × 1.5 mL tubes (≈50 µL per tube for 16 samples).

steps.title: Add primary antibody
steps.instruction: Add 0.5–1 µL primary antibody per sample (typically 1:50–1:100 dilution as recommended for immunofluorescence) and vortex gently to mix.

steps.title: Incubate primary antibody
steps.instruction: Nutate or rotate the tubes at room temperature for 2 h, or alternatively incubate overnight (or up to several days) at 4 °C; keep the liquid at the bottom and on the side of the tube while rocking.

steps.title: Remove primary antibody
steps.instruction: After a brief spin (<100 × g) to collect liquid, place tubes on a magnetic stand, allow beads to clear, and withdraw the supernatant.

steps.title: Add secondary antibody
steps.instruction: Prepare secondary antibody at 1:100 dilution in Dig‑wash buffer, add 100 µL per sample while gently vortexing to dislodge beads from the tube walls.

steps.title: Incubate secondary antibody
steps.instruction: Place the tubes on a nutator at room temperature for 30–60 min.

steps.title: Wash after secondary antibody
steps.instruction: After a quick spin, place tubes on a magnetic stand, clear beads, withdraw liquid, add 1 mL Dig‑wash buffer, invert 10 × or vortex gently to resuspend beads, then repeat this wash two more times (total three washes).

steps.title: Prepare pA‑Tn5 mix
steps.instruction: Dilute the pA‑Tn5 adapter complex in Dig‑300 buffer to a final 1:250 dilution, preparing 100 µL per sample.

steps.title: Add pA‑Tn5
steps.instruction: After a quick spin, place tubes on the magnet, clear beads, withdraw liquid, then squirt 100 µL of the pA‑Tn5 mix into each tube while gently vortexing to dislodge beads.

steps.title: Incubate pA‑Tn5
steps.instruction: Place the tubes on a nutator at room temperature for 1 h.

steps.title: Wash after pA‑Tn5
steps.instruction: After a quick spin, place tubes on the magnetic stand, clear beads, withdraw liquid, add 1 mL Dig‑300 buffer, invert 10 × or vortex gently, and repeat this wash two more times (total three washes).

steps.title: Tagmentation reaction
steps.instruction: Add 300 µL Tagmentation buffer to each tube while gently vortexing, then incubate at 37 °C for 1 h in a water bath or incubator.

steps.title: Stop tagmentation and digest
steps.instruction: Add 10 µL 0.5 M EDTA, 3 µL 10 % SDS, and 2.5 µL 20 mg mL⁻¹ Proteinase K to each sample, vortex at full speed for ~2 s, then incubate at 55 °C for 1 h to digest proteins and reverse cross‑links.

steps.title: Phenol‑chloroform extraction
steps.instruction: Add 300 µL phenol‑chloroform‑isoamyl alcohol (PCI) to each tube, vortex full speed ~2 s (do not separate beads), transfer the mixture to a phase‑lock tube, and centrifuge 3 min at room temperature, 16 000 × g. Add 300 µL chloroform, invert ~10 × (do not vortex), centrifuge 3 min at room temperature, 16 000 × g, then transfer the aqueous layer to a fresh 1.5 mL tube containing 750 µL 100 % ethanol, mix by pipetting.

steps.title: Precipitate DNA
steps.instruction: Place the tube on ice and centrifuge ≥10 min at 4 °C, 16 000 × g; carefully pour off supernatant, then rinse the pellet with 1 mL 100 % ethanol, centrifuge 1 min at 4 °C, 16 000 × g, pour off ethanol, and air‑dry the pellet.

steps.title: Resuspend DNA
steps.instruction: Add 25–30 µL 1 mM Tris‑HCl pH 8.0, 0.1 mM EDTA to the dried pellet, vortex at full speed until fully dissolved.

steps.title: Set up PCR
steps.instruction: In a thin‑wall 0.5 mL PCR tube combine 21 µL DNA, 2 µL 10 µM universal (i5) primer, 2 µL 10 µM uniquely barcoded (i7) primer, and 25 µL NEBNext HiFi 2× PCR Master Mix. Mix, quick‑spin, and place in a thermocycler.

steps.title: PCR amplification
steps.instruction: Run the following program: 72 °C 5 min (gap‑fill); 98 °C 30 s; 98 °C 10 s; 63 °C 10 s; repeat steps 98 °C 10 s / 63 °C 10 s for 13 cycles; 72 °C 1 min; hold at 8 °C. (12–14 cycles are recommended; use a 10 s combined annealing/extension at 60–63 °C.)

steps.title: SPRI bead cleanup – bind
steps.instruction: After PCR, add 1.3× volume (65 µL) SPRI bead slurry to each reaction, mix by pipetting up and down, and incubate at room temperature 5–10 min.

steps.title: SPRI bead cleanup – wash
steps.instruction: Place tubes on a magnetic stand, allow beads to clear, then add 200 µL 80 % ethanol without disturbing beads, withdraw liquid to the bottom of the tube, repeat the ethanol wash once more, then perform a quick spin and remove remaining liquid with a 20 µL pipette. Do not air‑dry the beads.

steps.title: Elute purified library
steps.instruction: Remove tubes from the magnet, add 25 µL 10 mM Tris‑HCl pH 8.0, vortex, incubate 5 min, place on magnet for 5 min, then transfer the clear supernatant to a fresh 0.5 mL tube.

steps.title: Library quality control
steps.instruction: Determine library size distribution and concentration using an Agilent 4200 TapeStation with D1000 reagents (or equivalent).

steps.title: Pool barcoded libraries
steps.instruction: Mix barcoded libraries to achieve equal representation as desired, aiming for the final concentration recommended by the sequencing manufacturer; perform an additional SPRI bead cleanup if needed to remove residual PCR primers.

steps.title: Sequencing
steps.instruction: Perform paired‑end Illumina sequencing on the pooled libraries (e.g., PE 25 × 25 on a HiSeq 2500 with 1 % Phi‑X spike‑in).
